structured_output.world_model:
Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.1 s) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a large memory-bound part on the 31×31 maps (whitening output and group 1: BN/GELU/pool). Accuracy rises slowly with total steps (~0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, ~1.5–2.7 s/pp). Tip E036 is 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Fresh seeds 13–22 gave 0.7525 for this recipe, so the population mean is ~0.752–0.753. That is only ~0.2–0.3 pp over the 0.75 bar, so the tip sits at the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Memory-bound cuts save more than their MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The annealed group-1 LR makes a freeze at 75% nearly free in accuracy. E037 shows the dose is nonlinear: a 60% freeze cost ~0.4 pp for ~0.25 s. 75% is near the knee.
3. Averaging, LS, warmup and Lookahead-interval tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative, by 0.2–0.7 pp. The recipe sits in a narrow local optimum. Any non-systems change should be shaded ~−0.1 pp.
4. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems work is worth ~1% each (CUDA graphs, prepare cost). Remaining systems levers are ≲0.1–0.15 s each.
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs ~0.4 pp for ~0.5 s, worse than the epoch dial.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE ~0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE ~0.06 pp. Time noise ±0.03 s. Any RNG change re-rolls seeds 0–2. Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse of ~0.05–0.1 pp.

Misses: I mispredicted the time of E034 and E037 (memory-bound savings are larger than I modelled), and the accuracy cost of the deeper freeze.

Unsure: the true tip mean; BN-folding dynamics; the PCIe transfer of bandwidth-bound levers. Dropping Muon (I059) likely costs accuracy, since Muon was a gain at E006.

forecasts.reason: Folding removes BN stats passes on the 31x31 maps for 25% of steps, saving ~0.1 s. Accuracy is roughly neutral, but the tip has no margin and the implementation is risky.
Diagnostic with no recipe change. The profile likely shows non-GEMM kernels at 30% or more of the step, and the tip's numbers stay unchanged.
Swapping Muon for SGD saves ~3% of time but likely loses 0.2-0.5 pp, so the tip falls below the bar.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean at least 0.752? Pooled seeds 3-22 would settle whether any further time cut is feasible.
How much of the frozen-phase step is BN and elementwise traffic on the 31x31 maps? That sets the value of I057.
Does Muon beat Nesterov SGD at fixed batch 2000 on held-out seeds? That decides whether I059 loses at least 0.3 pp.
